bihar_raw_news.content: ScanX News Regaal Resources turbine damage disrupts Bihar operations for ~35 days Regaal Resources turbine damage disrupts Bihar operations for ~35 days 1 min read | Published on 10 Sept 2026, 08:00 PM | Updated on 10 Sept 2026, 08:00 PM Reviewed by Naman S ScanX News Team Add as a preferred source on Google Key Highlights Turbine rotor and fan damage detected at new 825 TPD Bihar facility on August 26, 2026 Repair costs estimated at ₹90 lakhs, fully covered by insurance Operations expected to resume within ~35 days, by September 30, 2026 Unit was running at 50% capacity; existing orders unaffected due to stock availability powered by *this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only. Regaal Resources disclosed operational disruption at its newly commissioned 825 TPD facility in Kishanganj, Bihar, following damage to a 10 MW turbine. The company estimates repair costs at ₹90 lakhs and expects the unit to resume operations by September 30, 2026. The disruption stems from damage detected in the rotor and fan of one turbine on August 26, 2026. While initial assessments suggested minor repairs, detailed evaluation during the process indicated a longer timeline. The company confirmed that other manufacturing operations remain unaffected. Operational Impact The affected turbine is part of the facility commissioned on May 26, 2026. At the time of the incident, this new unit was operating at approximately 50% capacity utilization . The outage means this additional capacity will remain idle for the repair period. Despite the halt in production from this specific line, Regaal Resources stated it holds sufficient stock to service existing and ongoing orders. The company emphasized that current order fulfillment remains unaffected by the temporary loss of capacity. Financial Implications The estimated cost to repair the rotor and fan is approximately ₹90 lakhs . The company noted that this loss/damage is covered by insurance. It is currently assessing the broader extent of operational and financial damage resulting from the incident. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Ensures Timely Pension Delivery via DBT: A Commitment to Social Security
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Ensures Timely Pension Delivery via DBT: A Commitment to Social Security Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced the transfer of social security pensions through Direct Benefit Transfer on the 10th of every month. With 98,896 new beneficiaries added, the government aims to ensure equal social security benefits. Infrastructure and health initiatives were also highlighted during the event in Munger. Devdiscourse News Desk | Updated: 10-09-2026 19:07 IST | Created: 10-09-2026 19:07 IST Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary (Photo/ANI). Image Credit: ANI Country: India SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... In a strategic move to ensure timely delivery of benefits, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has declared that the pension amount under the state's social security schemes will be deposited into beneficiaries' bank accounts via Direct Benefit Transfer on the 10th day of each month. Speaking at a significant event in Munger's Haveli Kharagpur, Choudhary disclosed the disbursement of Rs 1,233.87 crore as the pension for August 2026, benefiting 105.68 lakh people at Rs 1,100 per beneficiary. This initiative sees the inclusion of 98,896 new beneficiaries in the social security pension scheme, reflecting the state government's dedication to deliver benefits devoid of discrimination. Asserting the administration's objective, Choudhary stated, "Ensuring the timely deposit of pensions into the beneficiaries' accounts is our utmost priority," emphasizing equal access to support regardless of caste, religion, or other distinctions. The event also marked the commencement of significant infrastructure projects, including widening a stretch of National Highway-333 to enhance connectivity in Munger and neighboring regions. Furthermore, Choudhary elaborated on plans to negotiate water rights within the Farakka Water Agreement and initiatives to develop tourism and healthcare across Bihar, underscoring the state's vision for comprehensive growth and welfare. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar govt to transfer social security pension on 10th of every month through DBT - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar govt to transfer social security pension on 10th of every month through DBT: CM Samrat Choudhary ANI | Updated: Sep 10, 2026 19:03 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], September 10 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday announced that the pension amount under social security pension schemes will be transferred to the bank accounts of all beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) on the 10th of every month. Addressing a programme held at Gangta Mor in Munger 's Haveli Kharagpur, the Chief Minister transferred Rs 1,233.87 crore as pension for August 2026 through DBT to the bank accounts of 105.68 lakh beneficiaries at the rate of Rs 1,100 per person. 98,896 new beneficiaries have been added under the social security pension scheme this time. Choudhary said the state government is committed to providing social security to eligible people from all sections of society without any discrimination. "The timely transfer of pension amount into the accounts of beneficiaries is the government's priority, and for this, the 10th of every month has been fixed for pension payment," he said. The Chief Minister said no eligible person would face discrimination on the basis of caste, religion or any other factor, adding that the government's aim is to ensure that the benefits of schemes reach directly to the bank accounts of beneficiaries. During the programme, Choudhary also laid the foundation stone for the widening and strengthening work of National Highway-333 from kilometre 28.340 (Gangta) to kilometre 38.340 (Kohbarwa Mor) through remote mode. He said the project aims to make the route safer and more convenient, which would improve connectivity between Munger , Jamui and surrounding areas and accelerate development. The Chief Minister said efforts would be made to include provisions in the Farakka Water Agreement to ensure that Bihar can access water as per its requirements. He said better management of water resources is necessary in the interest of Bihar and highlighted the need to resolve the issue of silt accumulation in the Ganga River up to Farakka Barrage. Choudhary said the state government is also working towards developing the Munger -Jamui forest area under a project worth around Rs 150 crore. He said the Bhim Bandh area would be developed and beautified, with facilities such as trekking routes and hotels to attract tourists from across the country and abroad. He further informed that court facilities in Tarapur and Haveli Kharagpur would begin this month. The Chief Minister said health check-up campaigns are being conducted across Bihar from September 1 to November 30, under which around 6.5 crore people will be screened. He added that treatment facilities would also be arranged after the health check-ups. He also said that the 'Seva Sankalp Kayakalp Abhiyan' would begin from September 17 to improve infrastructure in schools and provide toilets in schools and Anganwadi centres where such facilities are unavailable. The programme was attended by state ministers, public representatives, senior government officials and other dignitaries. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar offers incentives to attract sugar, ethanol and CBG investments under 2026 policy
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Ethanol News Indian Sugar News Sugar News New Delhi: Bihar has unveiled its Sugarcane Industry Investment Promotion Policy 2026, offering capital grants and land concessions to attract investment in sugar mills, ethanol, cogeneration and compressed biogas (CBG) projects, Vedwrath Kumar, Joint Cane Commissioner, Government of Bihar, said at the Indian Sugar & Bio-energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) conference 2026. Kumar said the sugar and sugarcane based industry has a significant role in Bihar’s rural economy, supporting the livelihoods of farmers and workers across the state. He said government incentive packages introduced in 2006 and revised in 2014 had helped expand the state’s sugar milling capacity. According to Kumar, Bihar’s sugar mill crushing capacity has increased from 33,500 tonnes of cane per day (TCD) in 2005 to 65,450 TCD currently. Distillery capacity has also risen from 75 kilolitres per day (KLPD) to 530 KLPD, while sugar mills now generate 88.5 MW of power. He said Bihar offers a large agricultural base, an expanding sugarcane feedstock base, a young workforce and connectivity to major markets in eastern India as well as Nepal, Bangladesh and Bhutan. The state government is implementing five schemes covering sugarcane nurseries, cane mechanisation, seed development, expansion of sugarcane areas and promotion of organic fertilisers. Kumar said these programmes are intended to strengthen support for farmers alongside industrial investment. Under the Bihar Sugarcane Industry Investment Promotion Policy 2026, a new sugar mill with a minimum capacity of 3,500 TCD will be eligible for a capital grant of Rs 70 crore, with an additional grant linked to capacity above the minimum threshold. For distillery and ethanol units with a minimum capacity of 45 KLPD, the policy provides a capital grant of 15% of fixed capital investment, subject to a maximum of Rs 5 crore. A cogeneration power plant of at least 10 MW attached to a sugar mill will be eligible for a 20% grant, capped at Rs 15 crore. The policy also offers a 15% grant on fixed capital investment for CBG plants with a minimum capacity of 5 tonnes per day, subject to a maximum of Rs 5 crore. For land, the government will provide leases of up to 40 acres for 30 years at a token rate of Re 1. Kumar said the state plans to establish 25 sugar mills and ancillary units across Bihar. As prime land is limited, priority in land allocation will be given to investors submitting viable project proposals. He said the Sugarcane Industry Department would provide support through a project monitoring committee and investor facilitation desk, covering the process from preparation of the detailed project report to commissioning and subsequent stages. The proposed investor process includes preliminary facilitation, approval by the State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB), financial closure and document scrutiny, project verification and release of subsidies and financial assistance. Kumar urged prospective investors to submit proposals early to receive priority consideration. bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar parents disguise themselves as beggars, travel for months across states to trace their missing sons (AI generated image used for representation) An X post that is going viral claims that a couple from Bihar disguised themselves as beggars and spent months travelling across different cities in search of their two missing sons. According to the post, the family had moved to Mundra in Gujarat in search of work and was living there with their two boys, 14-year-old Rahul and 11-year-old Arpit. On January 15, both children reportedly left home to play but did not return. The parents allegedly searched nearby areas, contacted relatives and friends and approached the police, but initially failed to find any trace of the boys. Parents reportedly leave jobs to search across states Three months after the children disappeared, the couple reportedly began suspecting that their sons could have been taken by a beggar gang. The viral post claims that the parents then left their jobs and began travelling while posing as beggars themselves. Their search allegedly took them through several states, including Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh. Live Events — Malanggav4 (@Malanggav4) The couple is said to have spent months moving through different streets and locations while trying to gather information about their sons. According to the claim, they eventually received information that their elder son Rahul had links with a beggar gang. Elder son reportedly traced in Bikaner The parents allegedly followed the information to Bikaner in Rajasthan, where they were eventually able to locate Rahul. However, the search for their younger son Arpit continued, according to the X post. Around 15 days after Rahul was found, the parents reportedly received information that Arpit was in Howrah, West Bengal. They then travelled to Howrah and, according to the viral account, managed to find their younger son as well. Viral post says both boys were reunited with parents The post claims that the months-long search finally ended when the couple was reunited with both sons. According to the account, the parents had given up their jobs and normal lives while travelling across states in an effort to locate the children. Their decision to disguise themselves as beggars was described in the viral post as part of their attempt to move through different areas and search for clues without drawing attention. The account has since circulated widely on X, with the story focusing on the lengths the parents allegedly went to in order to find their children. However, the claims in the viral post, including the circumstances of the boys’ disappearance, the alleged involvement of a beggar gang and the details of how the children were traced, have not been independently verified from the information provided. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Needs Flexible Coal Generation As Its Prepares For Higher RE Integration: Prayassaur
bihar_raw_news.content: News Bihar Needs Flexible Coal Generation As Its Prepares For Higher RE Integration: Prayassaur The group has urged BERC to recognise a 40% technical minimum for coal plants, instead of retaining the 55% level specified in the draft code. Saur Energy Desk 10 Sep 2026 15:52 IST Follow Us Bihar Needs Flexible Coal Generation As Its Prepares For Higher RE Integration: Prayas Photograph: (AI) Prayas (Energy Group) has called for greater flexibility in Bihar’s coal-based power fleet as the state’s electricity system adapts to increasing integration of renewable energy, particularly solar. In its comments on the draft Bihar Electricity Grid Code 2026, submitted to the Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission (BERC), the energy-policy group said the state’s grid regulations should better reflect changing power-sector operations and the growing need for flexible generation. BERC published the draft grid code on August 7 and invited stakeholder comments. Advertisment A key recommendation from Prayas is to align Bihar’s grid code with the Central Electricity Authority’s (CEA) requirements for flexible operation of coal-based thermal power plants. The group has urged BERC to recognise a 40% technical minimum for coal plants, instead of retaining the 55% level specified in the draft code. Advertisment Impact of Increased Renewable Generation The recommendation has a direct renewable-energy integration angle. As solar and wind generation varies during the day, the amount of electricity that conventional generators need to supply also changes. Prayas said flexible and responsive operation of coal-based power plants is therefore becoming increasingly important in the context of the energy transition. Prayas has proposed that Bihar define peak and off-peak hours, as well as high- and low-demand seasons, based on net load rather than overall electricity demand. Net load effectively reflects the electricity requirement that remains after accounting for must-run generation such as solar and wind. The group said this approach would better capture the changing requirement for coal-based generation as renewable capacity expands. The group has suggested, as an illustrative framework, three months as a high-demand season and nine months as a low-demand season. It has also proposed four peak hours and 20 off-peak hours each day. Advertisment Under the suggested approach, thermal generators would receive greater weightage for availability during periods when net demand is highest. Prayas has proposed around 2.5 times the weightage per hour for fixed-cost recovery during peak hours in high-demand seasons, compared with 1.2 times during high-demand off-peak and low-demand peak periods and 0.8 times during low-demand off-peak periods. According to Prayas, such a mechanism would encourage thermal generators to remain available when they are most needed to balance the system, particularly during periods when renewable generation may not fully meet demand. Advertisment 40% minimum operation proposed for coal plants The group has also asked BERC to incorporate the 40% technical minimum prescribed under the CEA’s Flexible Operation of Coal-Based Thermal Generating Units Regulations, 2023. The CEA regulations require coal-based thermal generating units to develop flexible-operation capability, including operation at a minimum power level of 40% according to a phased implementation plan.

bihar_raw_news.title: At Least 6 Injured as Portion of Under-Construction Bridge Collapses in Bihar's Hajipur
bihar_raw_news.content: Updated 10 September 2026 at 14:57 IST At Least 6 Injured as Portion of Under-Construction Bridge Collapses in Bihar's Hajipur Namya Kapur India News 2 min read Follow : At Least 6 Injured as Portion of Under-Construction Bridge Collapses in Bihar's Hajipur | Image: Republic At least six people were injured after a portion of an under-construction bridge collapsed in Bihar’s Hajipur on Wednesday, triggering panic at the site and prompting authorities to launch a rescue operation. The incident took place while construction work was underway on the bridge. A section of the structure suddenly gave way, causing construction material and debris to fall. Several people present near the site were caught in the collapse and sustained injuries. After the incident, rescue and emergency teams rushed to the site, clearing debris and assisting the injured. The injured were subsequently taken to a nearby hospital for medical treatment. The exact condition of those injured is yet to be ascertained. Visuals from the incident site showed a portion of the unfinished bridge lying damaged, with debris scattered around the construction area. Locals and workers were also seen gathered near the site as rescue personnel carried out operations. Advertisement Authorities are expected to assess the structural damage and determine what led to the collapse. Officials will also examine whether all required safety protocols were followed at the construction site. The incident has raised concerns over construction safety and the quality of ongoing infrastructure work. Under-construction structures require strict adherence to safety standards, particularly when heavy construction materials and machinery are used on site. Advertisement The cause of the collapse has not yet been officially established. Authorities are expected to conduct a detailed investigation to ascertain whether the incident was caused by a structural defect, construction-related issue, or another factor. The latest incident comes amid continued infrastructure development across Bihar, where several major road and bridge projects are currently underway. Accidents involving construction sites have repeatedly highlighted the need for stringent safety measures and regular structural inspections. Further details regarding the identities of the injured, the extent of the damage and the exact circumstances surrounding the collapse are awaited. Authorities have also been urged to ensure that construction work at the site is carried out only after necessary safety checks are completed. Any lapses found during the investigation could lead to action against those responsible. More information is expected as officials continue to assess the situation and investigate the incident. bihar_raw_news.title: Gadkari to skip Mumbai-Goa highway opening, says 'ashamed' of project delay | India News
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / India News / Gadkari to skip Mumbai-Goa highway opening, says 'ashamed' of project delay Gadkari to skip Mumbai-Goa highway opening, says 'ashamed' of project delay With the Mumbai-Goa highway still facing delays, Gadkari has vowed to blacklist more contractors and suspend officials responsible for poor project execution Nitin Gadkari highlights the need for timely completion and better execution of major highway projects.(Photo:PTI) Sarjna Rai New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Sep 10 2026 | 11:25 AM IST Listen to This Article Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari on Wednesday said he would not attend the inauguration of the Mumbai-Goa highway as he was “ashamed” that the project had taken so long to complete. Speaking at the inauguration of a six-lane elevated road corridor at Porvorim near Panaji, Gadkari said he wants to set a record for blacklisting contractors and suspending officials responsible for delayed or poorly executed infrastructure projects, as he expressed frustration over the prolonged delay in widening the Mumbai-Goa highway. Mumbai-Goa highway: Gadkari to inspect project in October Gadkari said a meeting on the highway was held with officials on Tuesday and he was informed that around 93-94 per cent of the project had been completed. Rather than attending a formal inauguration, Gadkari said he would personally inspect the road when he travels from Mumbai to Goa by car in October, and assess whether the road had finally been made convenient for motorists and other travellers. The Mumbai-Goa highway widening project has faced repeated delays and missed several deadlines, with work beginning in 2010-11 and the original completion deadline set for 2016. bihar_raw_news.content: "Major achievement for entire Kosi region": Bihar CM after AAI floats tender for Saharsa Airport upgrade ANI | Updated: Sep 10, 2026 06:49 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], September 10 (ANI): In a significant boost to air connectivity in Bihar’s Kosi region , Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced that the Airports Authority of India (AAI) has issued a ₹42.52 crore tender for the development and upgradation of Saharsa Airport. The move is being seen as a major step towards bringing regular air services to the region. Sharing the development on X, the Chief Minister expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and said the airport project would strengthen connectivity for Saharsa and adjoining areas. “Historic step towards providing air connectivity to Saharsa! Gratitude to the country's illustrious Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi Ji. The AAI has published a tender of ₹42.52 crore for the development and upgradation of Saharsa Airport. This is a major achievement for the entire Kosi region ,” he said. According to the Chief Minister, the state government is providing 12 acres of land for the airport project at an estimated cost of ₹147 crore. The land transfer and proposed infrastructure development are expected to pave the way for faster air connectivity across the Kosi region . “12 acres of land is being provided by the state government at a cost of ₹147 crore. This will pave the way for swift air connectivity to the entire Kosi region , including Saharsa,” CM Samrat said. The upgrade of Saharsa Airport is likely to improve accessibility for residents, boost trade and tourism, and provide a new transportation link for one of Bihar’s key regions. national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 165 India calls on BRICS countries to expand opportunities for women-led enterprises in global trade
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal has called on BRICS countries to work together to expand opportunities for women entrepreneurs and women-led enterprises in international trade. Addressing the BRICS WBA Women-Led Development Conference in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal stressed the need for easier access to credit and markets, along with predictable business rules. The Commerce Minister said India is focused on empowering women through financial inclusion, education, skills and improved quality of life, with the aim of making them drivers of the country’s growth. He noted that nearly 300 million women in India have bank accounts, while collateral-free loans are provided to women seeking to start their own work, including those without a credit history. Mr Goyal also said around 100 million rural women are members of over nine million self-help groups under the ‘Lakhpati Didis’ initiative, aimed at ensuring women’s economic independence and greater contribution to India’s growth. Mr Goyal also urged governments to encourage women-owned enterprises to participate more actively in international expositions, conferences, seminars, exhibitions and business forums. Calling for greater engagement among BRICS countries, the minister said dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward towards a more prosperous future for member countries, partner countries and the world. He also highlighted that India has set a target of growing from a four trillion dollar economy today to a thirty trillion dollar economy by 2047, when the country celebrates 100 years of Independence.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 178 India ramps up Nepal flood relief with 8th aid flight, specialised tunnel team and forensic experts
national_raw_news.content: India has intensified its humanitarian assistance to Nepal in the wake of devastating flash floods, delivering over 130 tonnes of relief material and deploying 54 expert personnel to support search, rescue, and forensic operations. The Indian Embassy in Nepal said yesterday that an eighth Indian Air Force aircraft carrying 35 tonnes of relief and rescue supplies landed in Kathmandu, marking the latest shipment in a continuous aid effort launched on August 26, 2026. India has also dispatched specialised technical gear, including mud rescue suits, gas detectors, breathing apparatus, inflatable walkways, portable generators, lighting towers, and dewatering pumps. India has provided DNA kits, reagents, and equipment for DNA profiling to aid in victim identification. Earlier, the Ministry of External Affairs also noted the handing over of the relief aid by Indian Ambassador Naveen Srivastava to Nepal’s Minister Mahabir Pun upon the arrival of the eighth aircraft. Meanwhile, India’s specialised tunnel rescue team initially launched joint operations with the Nepali Army across two high-risk sites in Chilime and Langtang. Search efforts are currently concentrated at the Chilime tunnel, where rescue workers face severe operational hurdles due to rugged terrain, constrained access, and steep tunnel inclines. Teams are currently constructing a makeshift access path to transport heavy machinery, such as excavators, directly to the tunnel entrance. Construction on the track is progressing steadily and is expected to be completed within two to three days.

national_raw_news.title: Mizoram CM calls for strengthening Irrigation & Water Resources Department 3 hours ago 38
national_raw_news.content: Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma has called for strengthening the Irrigation and Water Resources Department (IWRD), citing its expanding responsibilities and persistent shortage of manpower and technical expertise, official sources said. Lalduhoma made the remarks yesterday while chairing a meeting at the to review measures to strengthen the department. IWRD Minister PC Vanlalruata and senior officials from the General Administration Department, DP&AR, Finance Department and IWRD attended the meeting. The Chief Minister said several departments had been functioning with inadequate manpower for years and could weaken further because of staff shortages. He said the IWRD had remained in virtually the same position for the past 19 years despite a significant expansion in its activities and responsibilities. The department, earlier known as the Minor Irrigation department, is now involved in irrigation development as well as river basin planning, springshed development, integrated water resources management, hydrological data management, flood management and warning systems, multipurpose reservoirs and groundwater development, he said. During the meeting, IWRD chief engineer K Hamleta presented proposals for strengthening the department and briefed the meeting on the proposed follow-up measures, the sources said. The discussions focused on addressing the department’s manpower and technical requirements in view of its expanding role, it said.
